title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover edge-case (cooldown + hysteresis)
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed a customer incident where brief latency spikes in a single region caused the SLO enforcer to repeatedly open circuit-breakers and trigger regional failover thrashing. This manifested as oscillating traffic between regions and elevated tail latency for several minutes. Root cause: the enforcer state machine had a race between the in-flight transition path and the region cooldown timer, and the hysteresis logic used an absolute threshold that did not account for transient bursts from rate-limited backends. This PR fixes two issues: (1) introduce per-region cooldown windows to prevent immediate re-failover after a failover, (2) smooth the hysteresis calculation by using an exponential moving average (EMA) for observed latency and a relative threshold instead of an absolute one, and (3) add a small state-machine fix to avoid duplicate circuit-breaker open events when multiple evaluations run concurrently. Changes: - add region_cooldown_seconds config with sensible defaults (30s->3m depending on tier) - switch latency threshold to EMA-based smoothing with configurable alpha - serialize state transitions with a lightweight mutex to avoid duplicate open events - add unit and integration tests that simulate transient bursts - add observability: new metrics slo_enforcer.region_cooldown_started and slo_enforcer.hysteresis_value Checklist: - [x] reproduce locally with synthetic latency generator - [x] add unit tests for state-machine and EMA - [x] add integration test that runs failover simulation in test harness - [x] update docs/config defaults - [x] run canary in staging and observe stable behavior Notes: This is a hotfix intended to be backported to the 2026-02 release branch if approved. The change is conservative (defaults preserve current behavior for low-risk customers) and guarded by feature flag slo_enforcer.enable_ema_hysteresis.

Impact: reduced failover oscillation during short backend bursts; no behavior change unless feature flag enabled or config adjusted.
